Primary residential sales reached 8,146 units YTD (+47.8%), driven by mainland Chinese buyers and capital inflows, with Knight Frank forecasting full-year price growth of 8–10%. Retail sales extended an 11-consecutive-month growth streak with 12.8% YoY growth in March, led by motor vehicles and luxury goods.

title: Asia Pacific Investment Quarterly Q1 2026
summary: Asia Pacific real estate investment rose 19.2% year-on-year in Q1 2026, led by prime office investment (up 25.7% YoY) in gateway cities such as Tokyo and Singapore. Cross-border capital flows strengthened, with Singapore recording S$11.48 billion in investment sales (up ~95% YoY) and Japan's prime office rents in the Central 5 Wards reaching new highs. Data centre and industrial/logistics assets continued attracting capital driven by AI infrastructure demand, semiconductor exports, and supply-chain reshoring.

title: Japan / Tokyo Office Market – APAC Investment Quarterly Q1/2026 Highlights
summary: In Japan's office market, strong occupier demand, limited supply, and positive yield spreads continued to support pricing in Q1 2026, with prime office rents in Tokyo's Central 5 Wards touching new highs. Japan's commercial real estate investment reached JPY2.043 trillion in Q1 2026, up 2% YoY and the highest first-quarter level on record. Cross-border capital flows concentrated heavily in Japan during the quarter.

title: Savills Impacts 2026 – AI's Implications for Real Estate
summary: Savills launched its Impacts 2026 research programme examining AI's broad implications for real estate demand and strategy. The report includes analysis of 'Deep Tech cities', whose economies grew 0.9 percentage points per year faster than their host countries over the past decade. Savills found that companies significantly using AI are about 4% more likely to expand headcount than shed staff, and that economic growth and business sentiment remain more significant drivers of office demand than AI displacement.

title: Hong Kong's Resurgence Reflects a New Wealth Order
summary: Hong Kong overtook Switzerland as the world's largest cross-border booking centre in 2025, with cross-border wealth rising 10.7% to US$2.9 trillion driven by mainland China flows and surging IPO activity (US$36 billion raised via HKEX in 2025, up 218% YoY). Singapore and the UAE complete the top three global cross-border wealth hubs. Asia-Pacific's role in the AI supply chain and equity market performance in Hong Kong and Japan is rapidly expanding the region's financial wealth.

title: Singapore Industrial Market Q1/2026
summary: Strata industrial sales in Singapore declined 17.5% QoQ to 335 deals in Q1 2026, the lowest quarterly total since 2020, amid a more cautious business environment. Buyer preferences shifted sharply toward longer land tenures, with freehold industrial assets rising 2.9% QoQ to S$876 per sq ft and 60-year leasehold assets up 1.4% QoQ to S$569 per sq ft, while 30-year leasehold assets dipped 0.6% QoQ to S$353 per sq ft. Prime warehouse and logistics rents increased 0.4% QoQ to S$1.83 per sq ft per month.

title: Singapore Residential Sales Market Q1/2026
summary: Singapore developers launched approximately 1,844 new private units in Q1 2026, down ~30% QoQ and 41.3% YoY, while sales totalled ~2,025 units as demand outpaced new supply for a second consecutive quarter. Strong take-up was seen at River Modern (410 of 455 sold), Pinery Residences (537 of 588), and Newport Residences (184 of 246). Private residential prices rose 0.3% QoQ, moderating from 0.6% in Q4 2025.

title: Australia Retail Market in Minutes – Q1 2026 / May 2026
summary: Australian retail investment volumes reached approximately A$4 billion in Q1 2026, the second consecutive quarter above that threshold, bringing rolling annual turnover to A$13.2 billion — up from A$9.9 billion a year earlier. Institutional capital accounted for 54% of acquisitions, while private and syndicated investors rose to 44%. Regional centres dominated at A$1.8 billion (nearly four times YoY), and neighbourhood centres rose 54% YoY, though large format retail was more selective.

title: Singapore Private Residential Rents Outlook 2026
summary: Savills expects Singapore private residential rents to remain broadly flat through 2026, supported by manageable supply additions and stable underlying demand despite global economic and geopolitical headwinds. In the URA rental index, overall non-landed rents rose 0.4% QoQ in Q1 2026, with CCR up 0.5% and OCR up 1.0%, while RCR posted a rare 0.2% decline — its first contraction since Q2 2024. Median rents for new leases showed broad-based increases across all regions.

title: Singapore Retail Vacancy Holds at 6.3% Amid Tight Supply Pipeline – Q1/2026
summary: Singapore's retail vacancy rate held steady at 6.3% in Q1 2026, despite softer leasing demand and rising tenant churn, as the constrained supply pipeline (427,000 sq ft projected for 2026) contained vacancy. Prime Orchard Area mall rents edged up 0.1% QoQ to S$23.60 per sq ft, while suburban rents rose 0.2% QoQ to S$14.90 per sq ft. The market is bifurcating, with well-located prime malls maintaining occupancy while secondary locations face growing leasing challenges.

title: Singapore Real Estate Investment Sales Q1/2026
summary: Singapore real estate investment sales surged to S$11.48 billion in Q1 2026, up 95.4% YoY from S$5.88 billion, supported by developer land replenishment, private wealth participation, and REIT asset recycling. Residential assets led by sector share at 38.5%, followed by industrial (25.7%) and commercial (17.8%). Savills revised its full-year 2026 investment sales projection upward to S$35–40 billion, from S$34 billion.

title: Singapore Private Residential Leasing Q1/2026
summary: Singapore's island-wide private residential leasing volumes rose 4.0% QoQ to 20,862 transactions in Q1 2026, recovering from a year-end seasonal dip. High-end non-landed rents rose 1.7% QoQ to S$6.15 per sq ft — the sixth consecutive quarter of luxury rental increases, with cumulative growth of 7% from the Q3 2024 trough. Savills expects private residential rental prices to remain broadly flat through 2026, underpinned by manageable supply additions of ~5,371 units.

title: Singapore Private Residential Vacancy Q1/2026
summary: Singapore's overall private residential vacancy rose 0.2 percentage points QoQ to 6.2% in Q1 2026, with islandwide vacant stock increasing 2.3% to 26,158 units despite only 911 new units completing the quarter. Performance diverged sharply: CCR vacancy fell from 8.8% to 8.2% as net demand improved in the city centre, while RCR and OCR both saw slight vacancy increases. Total completed private stock reached 424,165 units.

title: APAC Prime Residential Markets Diverge — Wealth Report 2026 Analysis
summary: Knight Frank analysis published May 2026 highlights widening divergence in APAC prime residential markets. Tokyo led all global luxury markets at +58.5% in 2025, while Greater China markets remained under pressure with Guangzhou down 12.2% and Hong Kong slipping 2.1%. Singapore's UHNW population is forecast to grow 46% by 2031 with luxury residential prices up 7.9% in 2025. Australia's billionaire population is forecast to grow 77% over five years.

title: Asia Pacific Real Assets Market Update – May 2026 (APREA)
summary: Savills APAC Capital Markets presented a regional real assets market update at the APREA conference in May 2026, noting that geopolitical developments in the Middle East are influencing investor sentiment without causing a fundamental market pullback. Prime assets are experiencing a 'flight to quality' dynamic tightening supply and pushing pricing, while capital deployment is becoming more selective across different APAC markets. Savills characterised the environment as 'disciplined conviction' rather than broad-based retreat.

title: Powering Property and Private Capital — Data Centre AI Infrastructure Analysis
summary: AI-driven data centre demand is creating one of the most capital-intensive development cycles in real estate history, with the IEA projecting global electricity demand from data centres to more than double to ~950 TWh by 2030. Knight Frank forecasts data centre capacity growth of almost 25% over the next two years, with $1.4–1.6 trillion of infrastructure investment required over five years. APAC is a key growth region with Japan, Singapore and Australia among the leading markets.

title: Savills plc Q1 2026 Trading Update – Asia Pacific Commentary
summary: Savills reported that Asia Pacific investment volumes increased 16% YoY on a constant currency basis in Q1 2026, with broad-based growth across major sectors and markets. The firm recorded a significant recovery in capital transaction revenues in its Asia Pacific region, including a particularly strong start to 2026 in Hong Kong and improvement in Mainland China. Savills maintained its full-year 2026 guidance while flagging Middle East geopolitical uncertainty as a key risk.

title: Hong Kong Office Market Q1/2026 – Prime Central Rental Forecast
summary: Savills forecasts prime Central office rents in Hong Kong to rise 5–7% in 2026, supported by tightening vacancy in the core Central submarket. Central Grade A rents rose approximately 3.5% in Q1 2026, with Central vacancy falling to around 9.9% by February — the lowest since 2023. Non-residential investment in Hong Kong was boosted by office and hotel deals, and investors explored hotel-to-student-accommodation repositioning opportunities.

title: Asia-Pacific Capital Markets Insights — Japan Focus Q1 2026
summary: Japan attracted US$6 billion in inbound capital in Q1 2026 — 43% above the 10-year quarterly average — driven by tight prime office vacancy and stable leasing demand. Tokyo office rents rose 22% YoY as Grade A vacancy approached near-zero levels, while retail rents rose 8%. Living sector volumes dominated at over 80% of APAC living investment in Q1 2026, and data centre demand is rapidly expanding with over 80% of 2026 capacity already pre-let.

title: Asia-Pacific Capital Markets Insights — South Korea Focus Q1 2026

Logistics assets accounted for 38.8% of activity, reflecting steady demand and moderating supply, with KKR's acquisition of the Shinsegae Food Hub for US$201.1 million as the headline deal. Office investment is stabilising after meaningful repricing, with domestic Korean capital dominating Seoul office activity.

title: Seoul Office Investment Market Q1/2026
summary: Seoul's office investment market registered KRW3.0 trillion in transactions in Q1 2026, up 13% YoY, though representing only about 14% of the record KRW21 trillion achieved in 2025. The largest deal was Korea Investment Real AMC's KRW1.2856 trillion acquisition of Seoul Square in the CBD. Prime office cap rates remained stable at mid-to-high 4% nominal, though rising government bond yields are narrowing spreads and could exert upward pressure.

title: Seoul Prime Office Vacancy Outlook Q2/2026 and Beyond
summary: Savills projects divergent vacancy trends across Seoul's major office districts as new CBD supply enters the market. CBD vacancy is expected to edge higher due to G1 Seoul and Rene Square completions, partially offset by expansions (Netflix, Bae Kim & Lee) and relocations at Grand Central. GBD vacancy should remain broadly stable despite tenant turnover, while YBD vacancy is set to rise short-term before improving as NH NongHyup Capital and Mirae Asset Securities take space at new buildings.

title: Global Luxury Retail Outlook 2026 – Hong Kong (Tsim Sha Tsui)

Hong Kong remained among the world's most active markets for new luxury store openings. The report noted slower rent growth in Hong Kong in 2025 compared to 2024's rebound.

title: Global Occupier Markets: Prime Office Costs – Q1 2026
summary: Global prime office occupier costs rose 0.7% in Q1 2026, bringing the 12-month increase to 5% and the two-year cumulative gain to 9.1%. Tokyo posted the sharpest quarterly rise of any APAC city ever recorded in the series (12.7% QoQ), driven by near-zero vacancy in top buildings and landlords raising headline rents. APAC overall saw a 0.4% increase, with Asian markets excluding China up 1.4% on average, while mainland Chinese hubs continued to decline 2%.

title: Global Occupier Markets: Prime Office Costs – Q1 2026 (Tokyo Focus)
summary: Tokyo recorded the sharpest quarterly increase in occupier costs (12.7% in Q1 2026) of any APAC city ever measured since the report's 2020 launch, driven by near-zero vacancy in top-tier office buildings, landlords raising headline rents, and Japan's sustained inflation above 2%. Gross rents across the top Tokyo buildings had been broadly flat from 2022–2024 but are now rising as corporate profitability improved and demand for premium offices intensified. Fewer completions are expected in 2026 than 2025, sustaining supply constraint.

title: Global Luxury Retail Outlook 2026 (Ninth Edition)
summary: Average prime luxury retail rents across 27 global destinations rose just 0.9% in 2025, down sharply from 6.6% in 2024. London's Bond Street displaced Hong Kong's Tsim Sha Tsui as the world's most expensive luxury retail market; Tsim Sha Tsui retained the title of Asia's priciest strip at US$22,000 per sq m annually (€16,160). Singapore outperformed the global average with 2% prime luxury rental growth in 2025 and remained in the global top 10 for luxury store openings, alongside Tokyo, Bangkok and Shanghai.

title: Global Luxury Retail Outlook 2026 – Singapore Highlights
summary: Singapore's luxury retail market achieved 2% prime rent growth in 2025, outperforming the global average of 0.9%, and remained among the world's top 10 destinations for new luxury store openings. Limited availability on prime retail streets such as Orchard Road and Marina Bay concentrated demand in a smaller number of flagship locations, supporting continued rental pressure. Singapore retained its appeal with ultra-high-net-worth individuals from the US, Germany, and other global wealth centres.

title: Australian Industrial Review Q1 2026
summary: East coast industrial vacancy edged up marginally to 3.9% in Q1 2026, with Sydney recording the tightest rate at 2.9%. New supply is contracting sharply — 2026 completions are forecast to fall a further 20% following a 19% decline in 2025, totalling 1.66 million sq m. Brisbane leads on annual prime effective rent growth at 9.2%, and the thinning development pipeline is expected to drive stronger absorption and rental gains across east coast markets.

The CBD recorded rents of KRW133,300 per pyeong (up 3.8% YoY) and YBD rents reached KRW112,900 per pyeong (up 1.7% YoY). Maintenance fees also rose 2.6% YoY to KRW48,400 per pyeong, broadly in line with CPI inflation of 2–3%.

Vacancy rates for both general industrial properties and modern logistics improved slightly. The Kowloon East submarket faces rising vacancies as narrowing rental differentials between industrial and office space prompt tenants to consolidate into offices.

Brisbane CBD led with 11.7% annual net effective rental growth. Core precincts outperformed significantly: Sydney Core surged 14.3% and Melbourne Eastern Core jumped 16.1% YoY, creating a 54% and 93% premium respectively over non-core CBD locations.

Morgan Stanley raised its 2026 Hong Kong home-price growth estimate to 12%, citing strong sell-through rates, declining inventory, and falling land supply. Momentum is driven by a resurgent IPO market, mainland Chinese wealth inflows, and expanded talent visa schemes.

title: Seoul Prime Office Market Monitor Q1/2026 – Vacancy and Absorption
summary: Seoul's prime office market recorded negative net absorption of -26,900 sq m in Q1 2026, pushing average vacancy up 0.4 percentage points QoQ to 4.0%. The CBD bore the brunt, with net absorption of -22,100 sq m and vacancy rising to 5.5%, while the Gangnam Business District was the only major submarket to post positive net absorption with vacancy stable at 1.7%. Redevelopment-driven relocations continued to shape YBD activity.

title: Seoul Prime Office Supply Outlook: New CBD Completions in 2026
summary: Seoul's CBD prime office market is seeing its first new supply since Grand Central's completion in 2020, with three developments scheduled for 2026: G1 Seoul (April), Rene Square (May), and EUL Tower (October). No additional prime completions are expected in 2027, making the 2026 pipeline critical for near-term vacancy and rent dynamics. Savills notes market attention is focused on leasing strategies for these assets and their impact on CBD vacancy.

title: Tokyo Residential Market Q1/2026 – Occupancy Update
summary: Occupancy rates across Tokyo's 23 Wards rose 0.6 percentage points QoQ to 96.8% in Q1 2026, driven by a return-to-office trend (companies offering remote work fell from 48.4% to 40.1% YoY). The central 5 wards recorded 96.4% occupancy, up 0.4 ppts both QoQ and YoY. Savills expects stable demographic fundamentals, the spring moving season, and rising condominium prices pushing renters into the leasing market to continue supporting demand.

title: APAC Real Estate Investment Q1 2026 — Capital Markets Analysis
summary: APAC real estate investment reached US$64.6 billion in Q1 2026, the strongest quarterly result since Q4 2021, as capital decisively shifted from price discovery to deployment. Cross-border volumes more than doubled YoY to US$22.4 billion, with sovereign wealth funds and institutional investors deploying US$12.8 billion combined (+50% YoY). Japan topped inbound capital attraction at US$6 billion, with Singapore cross-border volumes surging to US$5.7 billion from under US$1 billion a year earlier.

title: Central Leads Hong Kong Island Office Recovery — Q1 2026
summary: Premium Central continued to outperform the broader Hong Kong office market with 5.1% QoQ rental growth in Q1 2026, with Traditional Central and Admiralty also rising 5.7% and 2.6% respectively. Finance sector demand — particularly from traditional securities houses, asset management firms, and Middle Eastern banks — drove the recovery. Knight Frank expects leasing momentum to strengthen further in Q2 2026, broadening beyond Premium Central to include Traditional Central, Admiralty and Wan Chai.

CBRE projects full-year 2026 residential prices to rise approximately 8% to 10%, supported by easing supply pressures and developer confidence.

The report highlights resilient occupier demand, flight-to-quality trends in office markets, and strong RevPAR growth in APAC hotels.

Retail leasing activity continued to reflect ongoing tenant reshuffling, while imports and exports surged 41.2% and 35.8% YoY respectively, supporting industrial market activity.

Shorter lease renewal terms are becoming more common among technology firms as companies navigate economic uncertainty.

The office sector led at US$23.5 billion, a 46.7% YoY increase, reflecting selective reallocation into prime, income-resilient assets as capital transitions from price discovery to deployment.

title: Hong Kong Monthly Property Market Report – February 2026
summary: Knight Frank's February 2026 monthly report covers Hong Kong's office, residential and retail sectors. In the office sector, leasing trends from 2025 are continuing, with premium Grade-A offices in Central seeing rising occupancy and limited availability, driving rental increases in specific premium buildings. The primary residential market recorded 1,542 units in January, up 101% YoY, while retail sales for full-year 2025 amounted to HK$380.46 billion, a marginal 1% increase, with high-street leasing continuing to reflect softness.

title: Hong Kong Budget 2026-27 Response – Real Estate Implications
summary: Savills Research published its analysis of the Hong Kong Budget 2026-27, noting mixed short-term signals for property markets. The super-luxury residential segment was adversely affected by a stamp duty hike to 6.5% on properties above HK$100 million, while the commercial market may benefit from a stamp duty waiver on REIT-structured acquisitions. Medium-term housing supply was projected to fall to approximately 17,000 units annually, with the Northern Metropolis identified as the core growth engine.

title: Global Super-Prime Intelligence – Q4 2025
summary: Knight Frank's Global Super-Prime Intelligence report provides a quarterly review of super-prime residential markets globally, with coverage of key APAC cities including Hong Kong, Singapore and Tokyo. The Q4 2025 edition notes that Hong Kong saw one of the strongest upticks in super-prime sales, while Singapore continues to set price records but volume remains constrained by high stamp duty fees. Tokyo led global prime residential price growth with a 55.9% increase in the 12 months to Q3 2025.

title: CBRE's 2026 Asia Pacific Real Estate Outlook Press Release
summary: CBRE's press release accompanying the 2026 APAC Market Outlook reiterates a 5–10% year-on-year increase in commercial real estate investment volume for the region, with offices ranked as investors' top preferred sector for the first time since 2020. Regional Grade A office supply is forecast to peak in 2026 at 61.3 million sq ft, with more than three quarters concentrated in India and mainland China, while developed markets such as Tokyo, Singapore and Australian CBDs benefit from structurally constrained supply. The logistics sector faces moderating rental growth as occupiers adopt selective expansion strategies ahead of a sharp decline in new completions from 2027.

title: Melbourne Residential Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Melbourne's inner apartment market hit a 10-year low in new completions in 2025 at just over 2,000 units, though supply is forecast to nearly double to approximately 4,000 completions in 2026. The median apartment sale price closed 2025 at AUD 615,000, largely unchanged since early 2023, while median apartment rent recorded modest growth of 3.6% year-on-year. Melbourne's rental vacancy rate reached 2.0% in Q4 2025, approaching its long-term average of 2.3%, with relative affordability versus other Australian cities expected to sustain strong transactional activity.

title: 2026 Asia Pacific Investor Intentions Survey: Japan Results
summary: CBRE's Japan-specific results from the 2026 Asia Pacific Investor Intentions Survey indicate that the Japan investment market will remain active, with many investors expecting real estate prices to rise. A pronounced shift from core to value-add strategies was recorded, as rising interest rates are offset by strong rental growth prospects in the office sector. Investors are expected to focus on achieving returns through rental growth that exceeds the impact of rising interest rates and inflation-driven cost increases.

title: Japan Multifamily Sector – Resilient Fundamentals Support 2026 Outlook
summary: Savills Investment Management highlighted Japan's multifamily residential sector as demonstrating resilient fundamentals entering 2026, underpinned by demographic trends, urban concentration, and strong preference for rental housing. The report noted that even amid Bank of Japan rate increases, risk-free rates would likely need to exceed 3.0% before cap rates broadly shift. Steady occupancy and predictable income were expected to continue supporting multifamily investor returns.

title: Savills Korea 2026 Market Seminar – Office & Logistics Outlook
summary: Savills Korea and Savills Investment Management co-hosted a seminar in Seoul attended by over 200 industry leaders. The seminar provided a comprehensive outlook for Korea's office and logistics markets, covering supply-demand dynamics, investment trends, and capital flows. Speakers also discussed European real estate equity and credit perspectives in the context of global capital allocation to Korea.

title: Tokyo Office Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Tokyo's Grade A office market recorded full-year net absorption of 124,700 sqm in 2025, a record-breaking level, driven by professional services, IT and manufacturing sectors. The Grade A vacancy rate declined a further 20 bps to 0.7% in Q4 2025, down 210 bps year-on-year, as Akasaka Trust Tower entered the market with near-full occupancy. Average monthly gross rent reached JPY 38,252 per tsubo, up 3.3% quarter-on-quarter and 9.4% year-on-year, with capital values rising 3.6% quarter-on-quarter and 13% year-on-year.
primeRent: JPY 38,252/tsubo/month

title: Tokyo Logistics & Industrial Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Greater Tokyo's prime logistics market saw its vacancy rate decline to 8.8% in Q4 2025, down 31 bps quarter-on-quarter and 74 bps year-on-year, as new supply fell below 100,000 sqm for the first time in eight years. Gross rents averaged JPY 4,780 per tsubo per month, up 1.2% quarter-on-quarter and 2.0% year-on-year, with prime locations showing stronger growth than fringe areas. Rents are expected to continue rising driven by 3PL and online retail demand, with cap rates projected to edge up only gradually.
primeRent: JPY 4,780/tsubo/month

title: Tokyo Retail Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Tokyo's prime retail markets of Ginza and Omotesando saw rents reach JPY 104,154 per tsubo per month in Q4 2025, up 1.9% quarter-on-quarter and 5.5% year-on-year, driven by international luxury brand expansion and strong inbound tourism. Capital values increased 1.7% quarter-on-quarter and 4.2% year-on-year as cap rates remained stable. Luxury goods sales resumed double-digit growth in November–December, with record foreign visitor arrivals supporting inbound consumption.
primeRent: JPY 104,154/tsubo/month

title: Seoul Office Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Seoul's Grade A office vacancy rate declined slightly to 4.6% in Q4 2025, down 13 bps quarter-on-quarter, remaining below 5% throughout the year, though the CBD held flat at 8.5% with scheduled move-ins pending. Net effective rent reached KRW 147,882 per pyeong, up 0.8% quarter-on-quarter and 4.7% year-on-year, with the quarter's office transaction volume reaching a record-breaking KRW 6.0 trillion. The largest transaction was Signature Tower in the CBD, sold from IGIS to KB Asset Management for KRW 1.0 trillion.
primeRent: KRW 147,882/pyeong

title: Seoul Logistics & Industrial Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: The Seoul Capital Area (SCA) prime logistics market recorded net absorption of 123,100 pyeong in Q4 2025, the highest level since Q4 2023, as annual absorption exceeded new supply for the first time in four years. Overall SCA vacancy declined to 15.2%, extending a four-quarter downward trend, while net effective rents reached KRW 32,400 per pyeong, rising 0.4% quarter-on-quarter. The logistics investment market surged to KRW 2.13 trillion in Q4, up 167% year-on-year, highlighted by KKR's KRW 1.03 trillion acquisition of Cheongna Logistics Center.
primeRent: KRW 32,400/pyeong

title: Seoul Retail Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Seoul's prime retail markets saw modest rent growth of 0.4% quarter-on-quarter for both shopping malls and high streets in Q4 2025, with Myeongdong recording the strongest quarterly growth at 1.0% driven by surging tourist volumes. Shopping mall vacancy improved marginally by 20 bps quarter-on-quarter to 1.1%, while high street vacancy improved 68 bps to 14.5%. Both shopping mall and high street yields remained flat at 6.6% and 6.3% respectively as significant yield adjustments remain unlikely in the fragmented transaction market.

title: Singapore Office Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Singapore's CBD investment grade office market gained further momentum in Q4 2025, recording its second consecutive quarter of over 1% quarterly rental growth—the strongest run since Q2 2024—supported by Singapore's economic resilience and broadening business recovery. No major office completions occurred in Q4 with the next significant delivery being Shaw Tower in 2026, while capital value growth accelerated alongside rents on improved financing conditions. The market is shifting to favour landlords in 2026 as declining vacancy and limited new supply underpin continued rental growth.

title: Singapore Logistics & Industrial Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Singapore's islandwide logistics and warehouse market remained stable in Q4 2025, with average rents unchanged for the sixth consecutive quarter, while healthy investor demand sustained steady capital values and yields. Demand for higher-specification logistics/warehouse spaces held firm from manufacturers, logistics service providers and e-commerce firms, with notable investment deals including CapitaLand Ascendas REIT's SGD 176.62 million acquisition of 2PS1. Full-year 2025 net space additions reached an eight-year high following the surge in completions in H1 2025, with rents expected to return to a modest growth trajectory in 2026.

title: Singapore Residential Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Singapore's prime non-landed residential market saw sales volume contract in Q4 2025, with October front-loaded by the launch of the 666-unit Skye at Holland. Prime resale non-landed home capital values rose on improved macro conditions and buyer preference for Prime assets as capital preservation vehicles. Luxury Prime rents fell amid weaker leasing demand while Typical Prime rents grew as cost-conscious tenants sought more affordable prime-district options.

title: Singapore Retail Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Singapore's retail market saw occupier demand soften in Q4 2025 as the challenging operating environment and shifting consumer behaviours led retailers to seek more affordable options, though the Formula One race and year-end festivities provided a temporary boost. Islandwide vacancy rose quarter-on-quarter but remained contained as landlords prioritised occupancy, while prime floor space rents held stable on continued demand from quality-seeking occupiers. The suburban submarket recorded the highest vacancy increase of 0.1 percentage points driven by closures of underperforming stores at non-prime locations.

title: Hong Kong Office Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Hong Kong's Grade A office market recorded its largest quarterly net absorption since 2019 at 1.5 million sq ft in Q4 2025, driven by pre-committed space at the newly completed International Gateway Centre in West Kowloon, with UBS and Banco Santander among the key tenants. The overall vacancy rate expanded to 14.1% as three major completions brought 2,659,300 sq ft of NFA to market, though Central recorded flat vacancy and Tsimshatsui contracted by 0.5 ppts. Overall rents increased 0.7% quarter-on-quarter in Q4 2025, with Central and Tsimshatsui rising 1.5% and 1.2% respectively, while Kowloon East dropped 1.2%.

title: Hong Kong Logistics & Industrial Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Hong Kong's prime warehouse vacancy rate rose to a record high of 10.1% in Q4 2025, up from 9.3% in Q3, as major retailers including Hitachi and H&M outsourced logistics operations to third-party providers, vacating large warehouse facilities. There were no new completions in Q4, with two enbloc warehouse transactions concluded—Big Orange in Tai Wai for HKD 500 million and G2000 Warehouse Building in Fanling for HKD 380 million, implying yields of approximately 4.5–4.9%. Retailers outsourcing in-house storage to 3PLs is expected to persist in 2026, keeping the storage leasing market challenging.

title: Hong Kong Residential Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Hong Kong's luxury residential market saw momentum in Q4 2025, with Mainland Chinese buyers remaining active in the primary market and Cullinan Sky Phase 2 selling out its first launch round. Luxury leasing market rental values rose 2.3% quarter-on-quarter on continued inflow of non-local talent and returning expats, while luxury residential capital values increased 0.2% quarter-on-quarter. JLL projects mass and luxury residential capital values to rise approximately 5% and remain stable respectively in 2026, with luxury rents projected to increase by 0–5%.

title: Hong Kong Retail Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Hong Kong's prime shopping centre vacancy improved marginally from 9.9% to 9.7% in Q4 2025, supported by increased rental concessions and seasonal demand, while high street shop vacancies rose from 9.7% to 10.0%. Total retail sales growth accelerated to 6.7% year-on-year in October–November, with electronics surging 30.2% on the iPhone 17 launch and banks and securities expanding on active markets. JLL projects high street shop rents to soften 0–5% in 2026, with prime shopping centre rents declining a further 5–10%.

title: Sydney Office Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Sydney CBD recorded its eighth straight quarter of positive demand in Q4 2025, with 20,500 sqm of positive net absorption driven by large-tenant demand across all four precincts. Sydney CBD core prime net face rents grew 1.5% over the quarter and 6.5% over the year to average AUD 1,540 per sqm per annum, with prime incentives reducing marginally to 32.8%. Two completions and four withdrawals were recorded in the CBD, with the vacancy rate expected to gradually fall over the near term as supply remains very limited.
primeRent: AUD 1,540/sqm p.a.

title: Asia Pacific Industrial Market Insights Q4 2025
summary: JLL's regional APAC industrial market overview for Q4 2025 reports net absorption increased 32.8% quarter-on-quarter, led by China Tier-2 cities, Southeast Asia and Seoul, though Tier-1 markets including Hong Kong, Sydney and Melbourne recorded negative net absorption. APAC vacancy fell slightly by 0.1 percentage points to 11.5%, while rents were weighed down by Greater China where landlords offered discounts, but remained mostly stable outside Greater China. Investment transaction volumes for the full year 2025 declined 18% year-on-year, though trended upward through the year, with Seoul mega-scale deals and Singapore portfolio transactions the highlights.

title: Sydney Residential Market Dynamics Q4 2025 (APPD Report)
summary: Sydney's inner apartment market saw its median sale price surpass AUD 800,000 in 2025, recording year-on-year growth of 4.5%, with the three-bedroom segment leading at 9.5% growth. The rental vacancy rate held steady at 1.4% in Q4 2025, well below the long-term average of 2.3%, while median apartment rent increased during the final quarter of 2025 to close the year 3.6% higher year-on-year at AUD 730 per week. JLL anticipates Sydney's apartment market is entering a period of renewed confidence in 2026, with supply-demand imbalances continuing to drive rental and sales price growth.
primeRent: AUD 730/week (median)

title: Asia Pacific Capital Tracker 2026 Outlook (Q4 2025 Edition)
summary: JLL's Q4 2025/2026 Outlook Capital Tracker reports full-year APAC CRE investment reached USD 147.6 billion in 2025, up 12% and the strongest annual performance since 2021, with Q4 alone reaching USD 40.3 billion. Japan set the pace with USD 41.4 billion for the full year, while the living sector captured a record share of APAC investment at USD 12.6 billion (+77% year-on-year). Looking ahead to 2026, JLL identifies prime offices in Singapore and Sydney, logistics hubs in South Korea and India, and multifamily in Japan as top investment picks, alongside growing interest in data centres and energy storage.

title: Korea Investment Market Review 2025 / Outlook 2026
summary: South Korea's commercial real estate investment market achieved a record-breaking KRW 6.0 trillion in Q4 2025 office transactions alone, with the full-year 2025 figure reaching USD 28.1 billion (+29% year-on-year). Domestic asset management companies with dry powder from NPS, Korea Post and Yellow Umbrella Mutual Aid are expected to actively drive the investment market in 2026, alongside continued foreign interest in logistics assets. The CBD supply pipeline is expected to create an additional risk premium for investors and may redirect appetite towards Yeouido and Gangnam submarkets.

title: Prime Residential World Cities Report – Seoul and Tokyo Lead Global Growth in 2026
summary: Savills' Prime Residential World Cities report forecast Seoul prime apartment prices to rise 6%–7.9% in 2026, following a 14.3% increase in 2025, making it the top-performing market globally. Tokyo was projected to see 4%–5.9% growth following a 30% surge in 2025. Singapore prime residential values were forecast to grow 2%–3.9%, while Hong Kong was also projected at 2%–3.9%. The report noted average prime capital values across 30 cities rose 1.8% in 2025.
primeRent: Seoul: US$1,730 psf; Tokyo: US$2,680 psf; Singapore: US$1,860 psf

title: Tokyo Office Market Outlook – Rents Set to Surpass Pre-Pandemic Levels in 2026
summary: Savills projected that Tokyo office rents across the Central Five Wards are on track to surpass pre-pandemic peak levels in 2026, supported by sustained tenant demand and diminishing availability of high-grade space. Rental growth was expected to be strongest for newly completed and top-tier office assets, while inflation-linked leases were anticipated to begin emerging in Tokyo from 2026. Supply was forecast to remain moderate through 2028.

title: Asia Pacific Commercial Real Estate Investment Reaches USD 40.3 Billion in Q4 2025
summary: JLL reports APAC commercial real estate investment volumes totalled USD 40.3 billion in Q4 2025, up 15% year-on-year, bringing full-year 2025 to USD 147.6 billion (+12%)—the strongest annual performance since 2021. Japan led as the region's most active market at USD 9.8 billion in Q4, while Hong Kong rebounded strongly with a 62% year-on-year increase to USD 2.4 billion in Q4. South Korea surged 41% year-on-year to USD 7.7 billion in Q4 on strong domestic office demand and foreign logistics interest.

title: Asia Pacific Data Centre Boom to Continue in 2026
summary: CBRE's viewpoint on the Asia Pacific data centre market outlines how AI implementation, cloud adoption and digitalisation are driving unprecedented demand heading into 2026, with aggregate hyperscaler CapEx forecasts exceeding USD 400 billion globally. Australia and Japan are set to lead demand, with Southeast Asia emerging as an investment hotspot as Malaysia, Thailand and Singapore expand capacity. Singapore's two new tranches of 1.2 GW development capacity will keep the city-state as a premium AI workload hub while pushing larger requirements to neighbouring markets.

title: 2026 Singapore Real Estate Market Outlook
summary: CBRE forecasts Singapore's GDP growth to slow to 1–3% in 2026, with firm occupier demand and limited supply supporting Core CBD Grade A office rent growth faster than 2025. Sustained demand and constrained supply should see prime logistics rents resume mild growth, while improving tourism and below-historical-average future retail supply will drive increases in prime retail rents. Singapore ranks among the top three investment destinations in APAC, supported by lower interest rates and a healthy pipeline of investment-grade assets.

title: Sydney Industrial Market Dynamics Q4 2025
summary: JLL's Q4 2025 Sydney industrial market report covers key leasing and vacancy trends across Sydney's precincts. The report covers gross take-up, new supply delivered, and rental movements across the Sydney metropolitan area's industrial submarkets. It forms part of JLL Australia's broader quarterly industrial market dynamics series published in early February 2026.

title: Global House Price Index – Q3 2025
summary: Knight Frank's Global House Price Index provides a quarterly update on mainstream residential price performance across 150 global cities. Published in early February 2026 covering Q3 2025 data, the report highlights that global luxury residential prices rose 3.2% in 2025, with Asia-Pacific markets performing strongly. Tokyo led with a 55.9% increase and Seoul followed with 25.2%, while Singapore and Australia both recorded positive performance, with six APAC cities appearing in the global top ten.

title: 2026 Asia Pacific Investor Intentions Survey
summary: CBRE's 2026 Asia Pacific Investor Intentions Survey of over 420 respondents found that net buying intentions improved to 17%, with offices overtaking industrial & logistics as the most preferred sector for investment for the first time in six years. Tokyo retained its position as the top cross-border investment destination for a seventh consecutive year, with Sydney in second place and Singapore and Seoul tied for third. Data centres were newly classified as a mainstream sector and ranked fourth in investor preference, with the strongest price appreciation expectations.

title: Japan Retail MarketView Q4 2025
summary: Japan's retail market remained extremely tight in Q4 2025, with average rents reaching record highs in three of 10 surveyed areas including Ginza, Omotesando/Harajuku and Shibuya. Three areas—Ginza, Shibuya and Sakae—reported zero vacancy in prime locations, reflecting fierce retailer competition for limited space. Persistent demand and a lack of available units are expected to maintain upward pressure on rents into 2026.
primeRent: JPY 299,500/month (Ginza, projected 2027)

title: Seoul Figures Q4 2025
summary: Seoul's commercial real estate investment market reached a record annual transaction volume of KRW 33.7 trillion in 2025, driven by office and logistics assets and an increase in owner-occupier acquisitions. Grade A office vacancy rose slightly to 3.3% while effective rents grew 6.3% year-on-year to KRW 38,304 per sqm, as landlords extended rent-free incentives. The logistics market entered a stabilisation phase with ambient logistics vacancy declining to approximately 10% following a 71% year-on-year drop in new supply.
primeRent: KRW 40,768/sqm

title: 2026 Asia Pacific Investor Intentions Survey – APAC Summary
summary: The 2026 APAC Investor Intentions Survey conducted in November–December 2025 shows net buying intentions reaching 17% (up from 13% in 2025 and 5% in 2024), with Korea, Australia and Singapore showing the strongest improvements. Core-plus and value-add strategies dominate, as investors seek rental growth-driven returns given limited yield compression room. Data centres were newly classified as a mainstream sector and ranked fourth, with investors expecting them to deliver the strongest price appreciation of any asset class in 2026.

title: Global Hotel Investment Outlook 2026
summary: JLL's Global Hotel Investment Outlook 2026 reports 2025 hotel investment volumes were up 22% from the 2023 trough, with international tourist arrivals surpassing pre-pandemic levels globally. The outlook for 2026 highlights improving liquidity dynamics across Asia Pacific, where RevPAR growth is leading global hotel performance. Strong debt markets, near-record dry powder and resilient sector fundamentals are expected to drive further growth in hotel transaction volumes through 2026.

title: Japan Office Market – Investment and Rental Growth amid Tight Supply
summary: Savills reported that Japan's office investment volumes reached JPY 2.1 trillion in the first three quarters of 2025, up 7% year-on-year. Prime office cap rates held firm at approximately 2.6%, reflecting sustained demand. Tokyo Central 5 Wards vacancy approached pre-pandemic lows, while limited floor plate availability enabled landlords to aggressively increase rents. New supply remains constrained by labour shortages and rising construction costs.

title: Australia Industrial & Logistics Market Update – Leasing Pivots to New Builds
summary: Savills Australia reported that leasing activity in the industrial sector was shifting back toward new-build facilities, with developer confidence firm in Brisbane and Melbourne. Vacancy rates for industrial buildings larger than 20,000 sq m averaged 3.5%, tightening from 3.7% the prior quarter. Speculative development was increasing across Sydney West, Melbourne West, and Brisbane Trade Coast corridors as occupiers prioritise modern specifications and ESG-compliant assets.

title: Japan Investment MarketView Q4 2025
summary: Japan's full-year 2025 commercial real estate investment volume reached a record-high JPY 6.5 trillion, up 31% year-on-year and 20% above the previous record set in 2007. Tokyo prime office expected NOI yields declined for the first time in approximately three years to 3.13%, establishing a new all-time low. J-REIT acquisition volume surged 2.7x year-on-year in Q4 driven by rising stock prices and portfolio reshuffling.

title: Singapore Real Estate Market Outlook 2026 – Webinar Key Trends
summary: CBRE Singapore's webinar accompanying the 2026 Outlook highlighted that Singapore continues to attract chipmakers, AI firms and global companies amid the AI CapEx boom. Rental growth is expected to remain steady across office, logistics and retail, supported by tight vacancy and resilient demand, with flight-to-quality continuing to define occupier decisions. Singapore ranks among the top three APAC investment destinations, with debt costs approaching the low 2% range following significant reductions in swap rates.

title: Singapore Residential Leasing Outlook 2026 – Rents Expected Broadly Flat
summary: Savills Singapore's residential leasing outlook for 2026 projected rents to remain broadly flat amid economic headwinds, stable supply, and subdued market churn. Alan Cheong, Executive Director of Research & Consultancy, noted that while the market remained resilient, geopolitical uncertainties and softening demand from some expatriate segments would limit rental upside during the year.

title: Hong Kong Residential and Office Market – January 2026 Update
summary: Savills Hong Kong noted that the office market showed a significant rebound in late 2025, with net absorption in Q4 2025 reaching approximately 984,000 sq ft — a seven-year high — driven by banking and financial sector leasing. Full-year 2025 absorption stood at approximately 1.6 million sq ft. The residential market was supported by low interest rates and the stock market wealth effect, with full-year 2025 residential transactions reaching approximately 62,000 units.

title: Tokyo Office Leasing Market Q4 2025 Briefing
summary: Savills Japan's Q4 2025 office leasing briefing highlighted that both Grade A and large-scale Grade B office rents in the Central Five Wards were on a positive trajectory approaching pre-pandemic peaks. Vacancy remained near pre-pandemic lows, with prime bayfront offices emerging as attractive alternatives as core area vacancy approached zero. Inflation-linked leases were expected to begin emerging in Tokyo from 2026, introducing a new framework for sustainable long-term rental growth.

title: Singapore Q4 2025 Residential Sales Briefing
summary: Savills Singapore published its Q4 2025 residential sales briefing, reporting that full-year 2025 investment sales totalled S$34.12 billion — a 27% increase year-on-year — supported by strong residential and commercial property sales. The luxury segment showed particular resilience, with 72 private residences sold for at least S$10 million in Q4 2025. Developer confidence improved following strong new launch performance, setting the stage for continued moderate price growth in 2026.

title: Data Centres Global Forecast Report 2026
summary: Knight Frank's Global Data Centres Forecast Report 2026 examines key trends driving the industry's evolution, including power availability, sustainability requirements and tech advancements, with coverage of EMEA, APAC and North America. For APAC, the report forecasts live IT capacity to grow from 14.5 GW in 2025 to 16.8 GW in 2026 (~15% YoY) and 19.8 GW in 2027, with Tokyo recording the largest ever data centre financing deal and over 80% of 2026 capacity already pre-let. Power availability is identified as the decisive constraint to further supply expansion.

title: 2026 Outlook for Hong Kong Island Grade-A Office Market: From Volatility to Opportunity
summary: This dedicated report examines the key demand drivers, occupier trends and market headwinds for the Hong Kong Island Grade-A office market heading into 2026. The report notes that premium Central Grade-A office buildings are expected to record positive rental growth of up to 8%, reflecting durable demand from financial services, family offices and Middle East capital diversifying into APAC hubs. A sharp reduction in new major supply from 2026 onward will provide the market with time to absorb leftover stock from 2024 and 2025.

title: Australian Capital View – February 2026
summary: Knight Frank Australia's monthly capital markets monitor breaks down the key indicators shaping the Australian capital markets environment. The report tracks investment activity across all major asset classes, noting that total Australian CRE investment volumes reached A$53.6 billion in 2025, the third strongest on record. Office transactions are rising, driven by end-user demand and growing investor interest, while the retail sector was a standout performer in 2025 with A$14.6 billion transacted.

title: Sydney CBD Office Market Report – February 2026
summary: Knight Frank's monthly snapshot of the Sydney CBD office market provides an overview of current market trends including vacancy, absorption, and rental performance. Prime vacancy is forecast to stabilise quickly as construction activity falls, with prime office rental growth expected to defy high vacancy rates. The development pipeline is thinning as asset values remain below replacement cost and rents are below the level required to trigger new development.

title: Melbourne CBD Office Market Report – February 2026
summary: Knight Frank's monthly snapshot of the Melbourne CBD office market highlights current market conditions including supply, demand and rental trends. Melbourne remains an attractive long-term investment proposition with the fastest growing population of any advanced global economy at 1.8% per year since 2000. Economic rents for premium towers are significantly above current and forecast rental levels, indicating a constraint on development feasibility that will limit new supply.

title: North Shore Office Market Report – February 2026
summary: Knight Frank's report highlights current and forecast conditions in the North Shore office market, comprising the precincts of North Sydney, St Leonards, Chatswood and Macquarie Park-North Ryde. The report assesses how metro corridor precincts are redefining the geography of demand as occupiers seek talent-accessible locations with strong public transport connectivity.

title: Leading Indicators – February 2026 (Singapore)
summary: Knight Frank Singapore's Leading Indicators report, authored by Chief Economist Ben Burston, provides key economic and financial metrics impacting property markets. The February 2026 edition tracks interest rate movements, employment data, GDP indicators and real estate market drivers relevant to the Singapore context, as global central banks near the end of their easing cycles.

title: Tokyo Data Centre Market – Investment Outlook 2026
summary: Knight Frank identifies Tokyo as a primary APAC data centre market where AI adoption is driving unprecedented demand. With over 80% of 2026 capacity pre-let, supply remains constrained by construction costs and power availability, driving activity including the largest ever data centre financing transaction in Japan. Investors and operators are forming new joint-venture platforms to scale exposure into digital infrastructure.

title: Japan Logistics MarketView Q4 2025
summary: Greater Tokyo's large multi-tenant logistics vacancy rate fell for a third consecutive quarter to 9.8% in Q4 2025, led by a 2.0 pp decline in the Ken-O-do area. Effective rents for Greater Tokyo increased by 0.2% quarter-on-quarter to JPY 4,490, while Greater Osaka vacancy fell to 4.2% with effective rents rising 0.7% to JPY 4,290. Greater Nagoya and Fukuoka also recorded vacancy declines as net absorption reached historically strong levels.
primeRent: JPY 4,490/tsubo

title: Brisbane Office Market Dynamics Q4 2025
summary: The Brisbane CBD office market recorded consistent demand in Q4 2025, reflected in strong net absorption figures. One project reached completion in the CBD during the quarter, and Brisbane recorded sustained and elevated rental growth through the period. The market outlook remains positive given the limited supply pipeline and continued flight-to-quality demand from occupiers.

title: Asia Pacific Real Estate Market Outlook 2026
summary: CBRE projects 5–10% growth in Asia Pacific commercial real estate investment volumes in 2026, as net buying intentions improve to 17% and offices overtake industrial & logistics as investors' top preferred sector for the first time since 2020. Office rents are expected to continue rising in developed markets such as Tokyo, Singapore and Australian CBDs where supply is structurally constrained, while logistics rental growth moderates as occupiers turn more selective. Data centres are ranked fourth among investor preferences and are expected to see the strongest price appreciation.

title: Japan Office MarketView Q4 2025
summary: Tokyo's All-Grade office vacancy rate dropped by 0.5 pp quarter-on-quarter to 1.6% in Q4 2025, with Grade A vacancy falling below 1% for the first time since Q3 2020. Grade A rents spiked 3.3% quarter-on-quarter to JPY 41,050, exceeding the JPY 40,000 threshold for the first time in 17 years. Rents rose across all grades in all 10 surveyed cities, with Fukuoka setting an all-time high.
primeRent: JPY 41,050/tsubo

title: Japan Real Estate Market Outlook 2026 (LinkedIn/Social Release)
summary: CBRE Japan's social media release of the Japan Market Outlook 2026 highlights that full-year 2025 investment volume is set to top JPY 6 trillion, establishing a new single-year record, with 2026 activity expected to remain close to 2025 levels. Office rents are projected to increase across all cities, logistics vacancy in Greater Tokyo is forecast to drop toward the 7% range by 2027, and retail markets remain extremely tight with vacancy at 0% in several key high street areas. Rising interest rates are noted as an accelerating factor but are not expected to dampen overall investment appetite given accommodative financial institutions and strong rental growth prospects.

title: CBRE Australia Pacific Market Outlook 2026 – Office Sector
summary: CBRE forecasts Australia's CBD office market net effective rents to grow +3.3% in 2026, with Brisbane (+7.3%) and Sydney (+6.6%) leading performance, while Melbourne's recovery is expected from 2027 onwards. Economic rents now exceed market rents by 20–35%, reinforcing pricing power for premium assets, and no new Sydney CBD supply is scheduled for 2026. Total office returns are forecast to exceed historical averages, led by Brisbane and Canberra, as cap rates remain broadly flattish before compressing in 2028.

title: CBRE Australia Pacific Market Outlook 2026 – Industrial & Logistics Sector
summary: CBRE's 2026 Pacific Market Outlook for industrial and logistics expects industrial vacancy to peak at 3.6% in H2 2026—still below equilibrium—before tightening further as new supply falls sharply from 2027. Effective rents are forecast to turn positive in 2026 as incentives stabilise, widening the gap between super prime and secondary assets. Rising e-commerce and hyperscale data centre demand are intensifying competition for industrial land, compressing developer margins.

title: CBRE Australia Pacific Market Outlook 2026 – Residential Sector
summary: CBRE's 2026 Pacific Market Outlook highlights Australia's living sector facing a structural supply shortfall, with apartment completions forecast at approximately 60,000 units annually—well below the long-run demand of 75–85k. Capital city vacancy is expected to decline from 1.8% in 2025 to 1.1% by 2030, with rents projected to grow +24% and capital values +28% over 2025–2030. Student accommodation and senior living remain under-penetrated, presenting significant investment opportunities amid demographic shifts and affordability pressures.

title: Regional Real Estate Forecasts for 2026 – Asia Pacific
summary: Savills World Research published its Asia Pacific 2026 regional outlook, forecasting a 7% rise in investment activity after broadly flat 2025 volumes. Tokyo Grade A office rental growth was forecast above 5%, Seoul investment was projected to grow 10%, and Australia investment was expected to rise nearly 20%. Cross-border investors continued to favour Japan, Australia, South Korea, and Singapore despite geopolitical risks.

title: 2026 Global Occupier Outlook – Asia Pacific Office and Retail
summary: Savills' global occupier survey found 89% of respondents forecast rising prime office rents in 2026, with Tokyo expected to see growth above 5% driven by near-zero vacancy. In Asia Pacific, India, Malaysia, and Vietnam were projected to see the strongest growth among talent hub markets. The report also found 82% of respondents expected increased occupier take-up, with a broad trend toward consolidation into fewer, higher-quality spaces.

title: 2026 Investment Outlook – Global Recovery to Strengthen
summary: Savills' global investment outlook for 2026 forecast global investment turnover to surpass $1 trillion, the highest since 2022, as stabilising values and improved institutional confidence drove deployment. Prime offices were identified as a leading investment pick among core/core-plus strategies, with living sectors and industrial and logistics remaining popular. In Asia Pacific, Japan and Australia were highlighted as priority markets for cross-border capital.

title: Asia Pacific Themes Shaping Real Estate in 2026
summary: Savills Impacts published its analysis of the key themes shaping Asia Pacific real estate in 2026, identifying the economic environment, AI and technology adoption, and geopolitics as the top drivers. Industrial and logistics sector was identified as particularly exposed to geopolitical risk from trade policy uncertainty, while office demand was expected to recover across major Asian gateway cities. Data centre and digital infrastructure investment was projected to continue accelerating across the region.

title: Pacific Real Estate Market Outlook 2026
summary: CBRE's Pacific Market Outlook for Australia and New Zealand forecasts below-trend economic growth of approximately 2% in 2026 and investment volume growth of ~5%, led by office and industrial sectors. Net effective office rents are forecast to grow +3.3% nationally, with Brisbane (+7.3%) and Sydney (+6.6%) leading the way, while industrial vacancy is expected to peak at 3.6% in H2 2026. The report introduces the 'TINA' (there is no alternative) thesis, highlighting how constrained supply across all sectors will drive returns over the medium term.

title: Singapore Residential Market Update Q4 2025
summary: Published in late January 2026, this quarterly bulletin reviews Q4 2025 performance in Singapore's residential market, examining prices and trends in the mainstream, prime and project sectors. Private home prices increased 3.4% for the full year 2025, coming in at the lower end of Knight Frank's projected range. Knight Frank anticipates private home price growth of 3–5% in 2026 as homebuyer demand remains intact amid global macroeconomic headwinds.

title: CBRE Korea 2026 Market Outlook Press Release
summary: CBRE Korea's press release for the 2026 Market Outlook highlights that 2025 saw a record KRW 33.8 trillion in commercial real estate transactions, with a partial adjustment expected in 2026 due to base effects but supported by strategic SI demand and alternative assets including data centres. Despite approximately 240,000 sqm of new office supply scheduled for 2026, vacancy rates are projected to remain stable below 5% underpinned by high five-day in-office attendance rates among Seoul occupiers. In logistics, new supply completions are expected to fall to approximately 860,000 sqm—significantly down from 2024—enabling average vacancy to stabilise in the low-teens.

title: Hong Kong Monthly Market Dynamics – January 2026
summary: Hong Kong's Grade A office leasing market recorded positive net absorption of 537,000 sq ft in December 2025, marking the ninth consecutive month of expansion—a clear sign of gradual recovery. The overall office vacancy rate edged up to 14.1% at end-December, reflecting abundant available space in the broader market, while prime areas such as Central and Tsimshatsui continued to tighten. Overall office rents rose 0.4% month-on-month in December, with Central recording a 0.6% increase.

title: Outlook 2026 – Asia-Pacific Office & Retail
summary: Savills Investment Management released its Asia-Pacific office and retail outlook for 2026, highlighting Tokyo's early expansion phase with Grade-A vacancy falling to approximately 1.4% in mid-2025. Corporate relocations and expansions drove record net absorption and rent increases across all grades. The report identified acquiring well-located but under-capitalised assets as a key strategy to benefit from the leasing recovery cycle.

title: Seoul CBD Office Supply Pipeline 2026–2032
summary: Savills Korea identified 26 new prime office projects totalling approximately 2.56 million sq m of GFA scheduled for completion between 2026 and 2032 in Seoul's CBD, equivalent to about 25% of existing prime office stock. The pipeline includes 11 trophy assets each exceeding 99,000 sq m. Delivery is heavily back-loaded, with only 13% of supply expected between 2026 and 2028 and over half due in 2029.

title: Seoul CBD Office Vacancy Outlook 2026–2028
summary: Savills Korea projected that vacancy rates in Seoul's CBD will remain low through 2028, with only approximately 343,000 sq m of new prime supply scheduled for the period — averaging 114,000 sq m annually. Historical annual net absorption in the CBD has averaged approximately 107,000 sq m over 25 years, suggesting upcoming completions will be readily absorbed. As of Q3 2025, the CBD vacancy rate stood at 5.0%.

title: Active Capital 2026
summary: Knight Frank's Active Capital Survey 2026 captures the views and investment intentions of 119 global real estate investors tracking US$144 billion of planned capital deployment. The survey finds that 87% of respondents by AUM plan to increase direct CRE investment in 2026, with offices re-emerging as the most targeted sector. In the Asia-Pacific region, Japan and Singapore stand out due to relatively low debt costs and structural demand drivers, with Australia also entering the top-ten destination list.

title: Australia Industrial and Logistics Figures Q4 2025
summary: Australia's gross industrial take-up in 2025 exceeded 2024 by over 10%, with the supply pipeline reaching 15% above the 10-year average. The national average super prime grade midpoint yield compressed marginally to 5.66%, while close to 50% of the 2026 supply pipeline is pre-committed. Net effective rent growth remained negative as incentive levels continued to rise across most markets, with stabilisation forecast for 2026.

title: Sydney Industrial and Logistics Figures Q4 2025
summary: Sydney's industrial gross take-up declined significantly quarter-on-quarter to approximately 95,000 sqm in Q4 2025, with transport, postal and warehousing leading demand at 56% of floorspace leased. The average vacancy rate rose marginally to 2.9% and super prime face rents recorded 2.6% year-on-year growth. Super prime midpoint yields tightened slightly to 5.17%, with AUD 624 million in investment sales recorded across 15 transactions.

title: Melbourne Industrial and Logistics Figures Q4 2025
summary: Melbourne industrial gross take-up declined quarter-on-quarter to approximately 190,000 sqm in Q4 2025, with the average vacancy rate rising to 4.7%. Average net effective rents continued to decline, falling 0.7% over the quarter as incentives remained elevated. Investment sales totalled approximately AUD 339 million across 13 transactions valued at or above AUD 5 million, with yields holding stable across all grades and precincts.

title: Brisbane Industrial and Logistics Figures Q4 2025
summary: Brisbane industrial gross take-up increased quarter-on-quarter in Q4 2025 to approximately 109,100 sqm, as occupiers sought functional and cost-effective solutions. Tight vacancy conditions continued to exert upward pressure on rents, with average net face rents increasing across all asset grades, and land values appreciating with 1.6ha lots rising approximately 5.9% quarter-on-quarter. Investment sale volumes totalled approximately AUD 336 million in Q4 2025, bringing the full-year 2025 total to AUD 2.8 billion—almost double the long-run average.

title: 2026 Korea Real Estate Market Outlook
summary: CBRE Korea forecasts 2026 as an inflection point for the Korean real estate market, with interest rate cuts and cyclical recovery converging. GDP growth is forecast to re-enter the 2% range and vacancy rates across Seoul's Grade A office market are expected to remain below 5% despite new supply entering core CBD locations. Investment volumes are projected to moderate 5–15% from 2025's record KRW 33.8 trillion due to base effects, while logistics supply falls to its lowest level in a decade.

title: Singapore Office Market Briefing Q4 2025 – CBD Grade A Rents at 2019 High
summary: Savills Singapore reported that CBD Grade A office rents reached S$10.02 per sq ft for the eighth consecutive quarter in Q4 2025, the highest level since 2019, while vacancy remained low at 6.6%. Based on tight supply conditions and sustained occupancy levels, Savills revised its 2026 office rental forecast upward to 3%–5% year-on-year growth. Strong pre-leasing activity and flight-to-quality demand were identified as key drivers.
