title: Australia Spotlight on 2026 – Commercial Property Outlook
summary: Savills Australia's Spotlight on 2026 report forecast more than AUD $50 billion in capital deployment, driven by a 'bull market mindset' among investors. Industrial and logistics assets were identified as the top sector of choice, with data centres benefiting from AI-driven demand. The report also projected a retail revival due to limited new supply and rising consumer demand, while prime offices in Sydney and Melbourne were forecast to see improving liquidity and early yield compression.

title: Seoul CBD Office Leasing Market Outlook H1 2026
summary: Savills reported that the Seoul office leasing market was expected to remain volatile through H1 2026 amid a sluggish economy, as major conglomerates including SK Group and LG Chem downsized or relocated to secondary buildings. In the CBD, notable departures were scheduled to contribute to a slight increase in vacancy, while in the GBD, Hyundai Motor Group's Global Business Center project targeted completion by December 2031. Three new prime CBD office buildings were scheduled for 2026 completion.

title: APAC Investment Outlook 2026 – Modest Recovery After Flat 2025
summary: Savills projected Asia Pacific real estate investment to rise 7% in 2026 after remaining broadly flat in 2025, representing more modest growth compared to forecasts for the US and Europe. Australia was expected to lead with nearly 20% investment growth, followed by South Korea at approximately 10%. Mainland China continued to weigh on total regional volumes, while Japan remained a strong destination for both domestic and cross-border capital.

title: Australia Data Centre Market Outlook 2026
summary: Savills Australia identified data centres as a standout sector within the industrial and alternative asset space for 2026, driven by AI adoption and data localisation demands. The Spotlight on 2026 report noted that competition for land and grid capacity was intensifying, while AI was unlocking record levels of capital. Savills expected data centre investment to remain strong, with industrial logistics and data centres as priority targets for institutional and cross-border investors.

title: Singapore Prime Non-Landed & Landed Residential Update H2 2025
summary: Published in mid-January 2026, this bi-annual bulletin reports on the market performance of Singapore's prime non-landed and landed residential properties for the second half of 2025. The report examines how easing interest rates are supporting prime residential demand, and notes Singapore continues to set price records in the luxury segment while volume remains constrained by high stamp duty.

title: Tokyo Office Market Outlook 2026
summary: Knight Frank identifies Tokyo as the region's tightest prime office market in 2026, with Grade-A vacancy in the five central wards tightening to near-zero levels. Tokyo office rents rose 22% YoY in Q1 2026, the fastest rental growth across the Asia-Pacific region. New supply for 2026 and beyond remains extremely scant and pre-leasing is well advanced on available buildings, while the cap rate hovers around 3.5% for core office transactions.

title: Tokyo Prime Residential Performance – Leading Global Markets
summary: Knight Frank's Prime Global Cities Index ranks Tokyo first among 46 global cities in prime residential price performance, with a 55.9% increase over the 12 months to Q3 2025. The outperformance is attributed to limited secondary market supply, strong foreign capital inflows and a persistent shortage of high-quality new developments. New condominium supply in 2026 is projected at approximately 23,000 units, the lowest level in more than 50 years, maintaining structural upward pressure.

title: Japan Capital Markets Outlook 2026
summary: Knight Frank highlights Japan as a core destination for global capital in 2026, driven by strong liquidity, low debt costs and strong inbound investor appetite following JPY 6.6 trillion in transaction volume in 2025. Q1 2026 volumes are 43% above the 10-year quarterly average. Japan accounts for over 80% of APAC living-sector volumes in Q1 2026, with new investors entering the multifamily market, while funding gaps in data centres are creating attractive private credit entry points.

title: Tokyo Retail Market Outlook 2026
summary: Knight Frank identifies Tokyo retail rents as rising at the fastest pace across the Asia-Pacific region in 2026, up approximately 8% YoY, driven by record inbound tourism and strong domestic consumption. Japan's high street retail market is experiencing near-zero vacancy in major corridors including Ginza, Omotesando and Shinjuku. Rising inbound tourism and the depreciated yen continue to support luxury retail leasing demand at prime high-street locations.

title: Japan Industrial & Logistics Market Outlook 2026
summary: Knight Frank highlights Tokyo's logistics sector as resilient in 2026, with strong demand and rent increases expected to offset rising interest rates as the market gradually sees more CPI-linked contracts. Renewal rates remain high amid tight availability of super-prime logistics space in Greater Tokyo, while solid domestic consumption and flight-to-quality continue to drive expansionary demand. Supply chain diversification trends are broadening logistics demand beyond the Greater Tokyo area to regional markets.

title: Seoul Office Market Outlook 2026
summary: Knight Frank identifies Seoul's Grade-A office market as supply-constrained, with the average vacancy rate across the three major business districts (CBD, Gangnam, Yeouido) at approximately 2.8% in Q1 2026. Tenants are adopting a wait-and-see stance ahead of large-scale new supply scheduled in the CBD in Q2 2026, including G1 Seoul and Re:nesquare. Rental growth is expected to persist as elevated development costs and rising asset values continue to widen the gap between prime and general Grade-A assets.

title: Seoul Capital Markets & Private Credit Outlook 2026
summary: Knight Frank highlights South Korea as a two-way bridge for private credit capital, with domestic institutions allocating to global funds while foreign investors target approximately US$325 million in local real estate credit opportunities. Korea's commercial real estate market enters a mild correction phase in 2026 after a record 2025, but prime office assets remain the core of transaction activity. Data centres, hotels and alternative living sectors are broadening the investable universe for domestic and international capital.

title: Seoul Industrial & Logistics Market Outlook 2026
summary: Knight Frank reports that the Greater Seoul logistics market is expected to see Grade-A supply fall to its lowest level in a decade in 2026, driving rapid vacancy stabilisation toward the low-10% range from approximately 17% in 2025. 3PL providers and e-commerce operators account for approximately 77% of total demand. Ambient-temperature logistics vacancy has already fallen below 10% and prime assets are experiencing rental growth and asset value differentiation.

title: Outlook 2026 – Asia-Pacific Living
summary: Savills Investment Management released its Asia-Pacific living sector outlook for 2026, covering multifamily, build-to-rent, and student housing markets. The report highlighted Japan and Hong Kong as markets with rising net migration supporting rental growth, and noted that throttled housing supply and lower vacancies signalled strong potential for rental appreciation across the region.

title: Hong Kong Property Market 2026 Forecasts
summary: Knight Frank Hong Kong's annual press briefing and forecast report covers the office, retail, residential, and capital markets sectors. The firm forecasts overall residential transaction volume to increase to 65,000–68,000 units in 2026, with mass residential prices rising 5–8%. Grade-A office rents on Hong Kong Island are forecast to decline 0–5%, with premium Central expected to record positive growth of up to 8%. Prime street shop rents are projected to rise 5–10%, while Kowloon office rents are forecast to decline 4–6%.

title: Hong Kong Major Report – Hong Kong Market Outlook 2026
summary: CBRE's comprehensive Hong Kong market outlook for 2026 forecasts that further interest rate cuts and a strong IPO pipeline will enhance the wealth effect, boosting private consumption and corporate real estate demand. Office leasing momentum is expected to improve, led by financial services firms in the Central CBD and the emerging Tsim Sha Tsui West cluster, while retail leasing benefits from student and tourist inflows. Commercial real estate investment volume is forecast to rise by approximately 5%, supported by mainland Chinese corporates and living-sector demand.

title: Hong Kong Property Market Review 2025 and Outlook for 2026
summary: Savills Hong Kong published its annual market review covering residential, office, retail, and logistics sectors. Executive Director Teresa Tang forecast residential price increases within 5% in 2026, supported by low interest rates and stock market wealth effects. Office rents were forecast to fluctuate narrowly within -1% to +1%, while full-year investment transactions were projected at around HK$40 billion.

title: Multiscale Analysis of Japan's Rental Apartments Market
summary: This research paper examines the factors driving investment concentration in the Greater Tokyo area, finding that Tokyo accounts for approximately 70% of total residential investment in Japan. The report identifies three key drivers: core investor criteria favouring Tokyo, high railway network density expanding suitable residential development areas, and rising university enrolment and urbanisation of employment. It notes a relative shortage of rental housing for low-income segments despite robust overall demand.

title: CBRE Hong Kong: Q4 2025 Market Review and 2026 Outlook Press Release
summary: CBRE's year-end Hong Kong press release reports that commercial real estate investment surged 130% quarter-on-quarter to HK$20.3 billion in Q4 2025, driven by mainland Chinese corporates and educational institutions, bringing full-year volume to HK$44.5 billion. Grade A office vacancy reached 17.3% after a wave of new supply, while rents edged up 0.6% quarter-on-quarter in Q4 for the first time since Q2 2019, led by Central (+3.7%) and Tsim Sha Tsui (+1.7%). Looking ahead to 2026, CBRE forecasts a modest 5% increase in investment volume, improving office leasing momentum, and continued retail rental growth of 5–7% in leading high streets.

title: 2026 Global Data Center Market Outlook
summary: JLL's annual data centre outlook forecasts global capacity to nearly double from 103 GW to 200 GW by 2030, with APAC expanding from 32 GW to 57 GW at a 12% CAGR. The report highlights a USD 3 trillion investment supercycle driven by AI demand, with colocation leading APAC growth at 19%. APAC lease rates are anticipated to increase at a 4% CAGR through 2030 as demand shifts from constrained markets to emerging hubs.

title: 2026 Global Data Center Outlook – APAC Highlights
summary: JLL's comprehensive 2026 data centre outlook highlights APAC-specific findings, noting that APAC data centre capacity will expand from 32 GW to 57 GW by 2030 at a 12% CAGR, with colocation leading growth at 19%. The report emphasises that 97% global occupancy and 77% of the construction pipeline pre-committed to tenants demonstrate healthy sector fundamentals without signs of a bubble. APAC lease rates are projected to increase at a 4% CAGR through 2030 as demand shifts from constrained core markets to emerging hubs.

title: Singapore Sales & Investment Report Q4 2025 / FY2025
summary: Savills Singapore reported that investment sales in Q4 2025 rose 44.4% year-on-year to approximately S$11 billion, marking a three-year high and driven by commercial and industrial transactions. Full-year 2025 investment sales totalled S$34.12 billion, up 27% from the prior year. Savills attributed the strong close to improved investor sentiment, lower financing costs, and capital recycling by developers and REITs.

title: Asia-Pacific Real Estate Outlook 2026: Hunting for Value amid Volatility
summary: Knight Frank's annual Asia-Pacific Outlook report positions 2026 as a year for disciplined value hunting across the region. APAC GDP is forecast to ease from 4.5% in 2025 to 4.1% in 2026, but the region will still account for more than half of global expansion. Prime Grade-A offices command rent premiums of 15–20% over Grade-B space in core APAC cities, and commercial real estate investment volumes are expected to rise a further 5–10% in 2026, building on a 9% increase in the first nine months of 2025.

title: Investment Yield Guide – January 2026 (Hong Kong)
summary: Knight Frank's monthly Hong Kong Investment Yield Guide provides a monthly update on prime yields across all commercial sectors and current market sentiment. The January 2026 edition reflects the market conditions entering 2026, covering office, retail, industrial and residential prime yield benchmarks across Hong Kong's key sub-markets including Central, Kowloon and the New Territories.

title: Korea: South Korea Emerges as a Two-Way Bridge for Private Credit Capital
summary: Part of Knight Frank's Asia-Pacific Horizon series, this article on South Korea examines how domestic institutions are allocating to global funds while foreign investors target approximately US$325 million in local private credit opportunities. Korea's real estate private credit market is identified as a compelling opportunity as traditional lenders approach exposure limits in high-conviction sectors such as data centres, creating attractive entry points for private credit and offshore capital.

title: Australia's Private Credit Market Set for Sustained Growth
summary: Part of Knight Frank's Asia-Pacific Horizon series, this report examines Australia's growing market for private credit in real estate. Major Australian lenders have halved their commercial real estate exposure since 2009, creating a US$33–56 billion opportunity for alternative lenders. Australia is expected to capture nearly half of the forecast US$90–110 billion expansion in Asia-Pacific real estate private credit by 2028.
